figures.caption: Figure 1: Comparison of the traditional MRAG pipeline (a) and our FES-RAG framework (b). Traditional methods only perform document-level retrieval and reranking, while our approach adds an additional document segmentation and fragment selection stage to purify the evidence.

Figure 5: Qualitative analysis of the FES-RAG framework. The selector effectively filters out semantically related but irrelevant fragments (Label=0) and prioritizes answer-critical evidence (Label=1) across both visual and textual modalities.

Table 1: Main comparison of FES-RAG-top5 against baselines across multiple MLLMs. FES-RAG utilizes fine-grained segmentation and distillation. The results show that FES-RAG consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance. Best results are in bold, second-best are underlined.

Figure 3: Impact of Knowledge Distillation. Comparison among three identical Jina-Reranker-2B student selectors: trained with hard labels (CE (No Teacher)), distilled from a same-size teacher (Same-Size KD using Qwen3-VL-2B), and distilled from the full teacher (FES-RAG using Qwen3VL-32B). The results confirm the intrinsic value of soft distribution-level distillation independent of model scaling.

Figure 2: Overview of the proposed FES-RAG framework. (a) FIG Calculation and Selector Training: During training, retrieved multimodal documents are decomposed into textual fragments via recursive binary segmentation and visual fragments via Grounding DINO. A frozen teacher MLLM estimates the Fragment Information Gain (FIG) of each fragment by comparing the likelihood of the ground-truth answer with and without the fragment. The resulting hard labels and teacher logits are then used to train a lightweight student selector through binary classification and knowledge distillation. (b) FES-RAG Inference Pipeline: During inference, FES-RAG first retrieves top-ranked documents and segments them into fine-grained textual and visual fragments. These fragments are combined with the remaining coarse-grained candidates to form a hybrid evidence pool. The trained student selector scores this pool and selects the top-𝐾 high-utility evidence units, which are fed to the MLLM generator as compact, purified context.
